In our case they also needed to remove our 13 year old system that had failed.I am extremely happy with the quality of work both for the old system removal and install of the new solar system and battery. Added a battery and additional panels to my existing system.Quote, sales and nstallation went seamlessly.Very professional crew. Able to answer all my questions and explained exactly how it worked.Installed the app and showed how it works.System is currently working great.
Rhys was very knowledgeable and helpful with regards to selecting a system for a new house. Installation was expediated to fit in with the build process. Very happy with the service provided
All staff I have interacted with have been professional and personable.Quality and very neat installation.Thank you.

I sought quotes from number of solar PV and battery system solution providers in the ACT, with Stag being the only one who supported me through the process of my attaining a better understanding of my requirements and the solutions that could be supplied to met those requirements. Talk about getting our battery installed before Christmas, fantastic job, lovely young man explained everything to me, and a great price for a 20 kw battery very happy with the service highly recommended.

Okay I’m revising my original review of Stag Electrical. The reason is while my angry rant made me feel better it wasn’t particularly helpful to others. I now recognise Stag was incredibly naive and unrealistically complacent rather than necessarily incompetent. And I have to accept that more assiduous work on my part may have helped to avoid the shambles this became.Just a recap: I sought quotes through SolarQuotes near the end of April 2025, and received 3 referrals. I ordered a Powerwall 2 and paid the deposit to Stag Electrical in early May. This was to be the second Powerwall for my system. No other battery (including other Tesla batteries) was compatible. If I failed to secure a Powerwall 2 then I was stuck with a substandard solution for the foreseeable future. Tesla ceased production of Powerwall 2s in 2024 and old stock was rapidly disappearing. On top of that the federal government had introduced the battery rebate! And in Canberra there were rumours that the government interest-free solar loans were going to cease on 30 June (which in fact did occur); while I wasn’t getting a loan this promoted even more demand for batteries. This was the proverbial perfect storm and to say it made me nervous is an understatement.I contacted all who quoted and expressed my concerns about my fear of Powerwall 2s disappearing in the frenetic buildup to the start of the federal battery rebate. They agreed with me and said they would bring  a Powerwall 2 into their stock as soon as I paid the deposit. One reason I am modifying my review is that I can’t recall Stag Electrical making that specific undertaking. I had assumed anyone who worked in the industry as long as Stag would do the same as other suppliers and physically secure the stock. But I don’t recall explicitly asking for this. My bad number one.I still think Stag could have, with minimal effort, secured a Powerwall 2 battery rather than rely on reserving one with a wholesaler who was obviously going to be under immense pressure to satisfy an unprecedented demand for stock to desperate installers. Just about everyone in the industry had predicted this. And Powerwall 2s were special in my case because I could not expand my system with any other battery.The second area where Stag let me down was implying my Powerwall was available in each of my follow-up phone calls. They were even offering assurances to me in June, although apparently now saying they found out (in July admittedly) that Powerwall 2s ceased to be available in May. I accepted those undertakings, again based on my previous dealings with Stag and SolarQuotes endorsement of them. My bad number 2.So on 1 July I was waiting for the call from Stag to tell me when my installation would occur. The call I got on 14 July was that Stag could not source a Powerwall 2 even though they had been trying for the past 2 weeks. I was not a happy camper to find out that not only had they not secured stock but had also been giving me assurances for the past 2 months that everything was on track. I may have overreacted a little.While the result was initially devastating for me, I have to concede that I could have been more explicit and rigorous in keeping Stag on track, and have to accept that.I still think Stag should have, as an experienced operator in the industry, done more to secure a battery without the need for a customer to constantly hassle them. But lessons learned.Just because an installer has provided good service in the past there is no guarantee they will continue to do so.SolarQuotes endorsement of an installer is a low bar and due diligence requires much more than relying on that.

We also needed a switchboard upgrade done as the switchboard in our house was old and at it's limit. We had been told by another electrician & a different solar company that the entire meterbox enclosure and all the equipment(excluding meters) required replacement. Thankfully Mitch looked at the pictures of the enclosure and informed us that it was in fact an appropriate size and would merely require the switchboard to be updated internally, saving us a good amount of money. After receiving a couple of quotes, STAG came out in front in both customer service and clarity of quote. They were not as cheap as the fly-by-night/cowboy operations however they were notably cheaper than another popular local company we had visit and quote. Their quoting package also included a finance option from Brighte which we used.We accepted their quote and went ahead on the evening of 1st of May, had contact 2nd of May to confirm NMI details and sort some paperwork then installation went ahead 7th of May which was fantastic. The team from STAG arrived when they said they would, went straight ahead with the installation and were done on the day (they informed me it was a very straightforward installation being a single story house with tin roof). Once the installation was done, they ran me through what they had done in the installation, the operating procedure for the inverter, set the inverter up and ran me through the app, which was already showing the power generated by the system. The installation was neat and tidy (there was an external conduit run which the installer said he would usually run inside the wall cavity however being an older house the cavity was not large enough to accomodate the wiring run - our neighbours install is very similar). They cleaned up after they were done and apart from the new inverter and switchboard in the meterbox (and of course the solar panels on the roof) there is no sign there were here afterwards.Everyone throughout the process was friendly, polite and helpful. I will be happy to recommend STAG to anyone I speak to about solar.
